next_state_election.source_name: New Jersey Division of Elections — Voter Information Portal

glance_notes.source_name: New Jersey Division of Elections — Register to Vote
glance_notes.text: 2026 General Election Registration Deadline: The voter registration deadline for New Jersey's November 3, 2026 General Election is October 13, 2026. New Jersey requires registration 21 days before an election and does not provide general Election Day voter registration.

glance_notes.source_name: New Jersey Division of Elections — In-Person Early Voting
glance_notes.text: Early Voting October 24–November 1: New Jersey's in-person early voting period for the November 3, 2026 General Election runs from October 24 through November 1. Early voting is available to registered voters at designated locations within their county.

glance_notes.source_name: New Jersey Division of Elections — Vote-By-Mail
glance_notes.text: No-Excuse Vote-by-Mail: Every active registered New Jersey voter is eligible to request a mail-in ballot without providing an excuse. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, counties begin mailing ballots by September 19.

register.label: Register to Vote
register.content: Eligible New Jersey residents may register online or submit a paper voter registration application to their County Commissioner of Registration or Superintendent of Elections. To register, a person must be a U.S. citizen, be at least 17 years old, be a resident of the county for at least 30 days before the election and not be serving a sentence of incarceration because of a conviction for an indictable offense. A person normally cannot vote until age 18, but a 17-year-old who will turn 18 by the following General Election may vote in that year's Primary Election. New Jersey restores voting eligibility after release from incarceration for an indictable offense; probation and parole do not by themselves prevent an otherwise eligible person from registering and voting.
register.source_name: New Jersey Division of Elections — Register to Vote
register.internal_note: The Division of Elections directly confirms citizenship, age, 30-day county residency and incarceration requirements. New Jersey's current felony-voting rule disqualifies a person only while serving a sentence of incarceration for an indictable offense. Older descriptions stating that probation or parole also disqualifies a voter are outdated. Online registration requires a date of birth plus qualifying MVC identification or a Social Security number and an electronic signature.

check_registration.label: Check Voter Registration
check_registration.content: Use New Jersey's official Voter Search through the Voter Information Portal to check whether your registration is current. Voters whose address or other registration information has changed should update their record before the registration deadline. County election officials can assist when registration information is missing or incorrect.
check_registration.glance_value: Check with the official Voter Search
check_registration.source_name: New Jersey Division of Elections — Register to Vote
check_registration.internal_note: The Division of Elections registration page directly links voters to the state's Am I Registered/Voter Search service. Inactive voters should update their records; the state notes that inactive voters do not receive sample ballots and are not eligible to receive a vote-by-mail ballot until returned to active status.

deadlines.label: Registration Deadlines
deadlines.content: The voter registration deadline for New Jersey's November 3, 2026 General Election is Tuesday, October 13, 2026, which is 21 days before Election Day. County Commissioners of Registration must provide evening voter registration from 4:00 p.m. until 9:00 p.m. on October 13. New Jersey does not provide general same-day or Election Day voter registration.
deadlines.source_name: New Jersey Division of Elections — 2026 General Election Timeline
deadlines.internal_note: The official 2026 General Election Timeline directly establishes October 13 as the registration deadline under N.J.S.A. 19:31-6 and mandatory 4:00 p.m.-9:00 p.m. registration hours at County Commissioners of Registration under N.J.S.A. 19:31-2. Municipal clerks may optionally provide the same evening registration service.

polling_place.label: Find a Polling Place
polling_place.content: Use New Jersey's official Polling Place Search Tool to find your assigned Election Day polling location. Polling-place information is supplied by the counties and may be updated before an election. A voter's polling location is also printed on the sample ballot sent by the county. Early voting uses separate designated county early-voting locations, so voters should verify the correct location for the day they plan to vote.
polling_place.glance_value: Use New Jersey's Polling Place Search Tool
polling_place.source_name: New Jersey Division of Elections — Election Day Polling Locations
polling_place.internal_note: The Division of Elections directly states that polling-location information is supplied by counties and is being updated. It also states that the polling location appears on the voter's sample ballot. Early-voting sites are separate and allow countywide early voting at designated locations.

election_day.label: Election Day Voting
election_day.content: New Jersey's General Election is Tuesday, November 3, 2026. Polling places are open from 6:00 a.m. until 8:00 p.m. Anyone who is in line when the polls close must be allowed to vote. New Jersey does not generally require an already-registered voter to present identification at the polling place. Certain first-time voters whose identification was not verified during registration must provide an accepted identifying document. A voter who requested a vote-by-mail ballot but then chooses to vote at an Election Day polling place may vote only by provisional paper ballot. Vote-by-mail ballots cannot be returned to an Election Day polling place.
election_day.source_name: New Jersey Division of Elections — Frequently Asked Questions
election_day.internal_note: The current 2026 voter materials directly establish 6:00 a.m.-8:00 p.m. Election Day voting. The 2026 Voters' Bill of Rights confirms that voters in line at closing must be allowed to vote and identifies the limited first-time-voter ID requirement. The early-voting FAQ confirms that a voter who applied for a vote-by-mail ballot may cast only a provisional ballot at the Election Day polling place if the voter has not already voted that mail ballot.

polling_hours.label: Polling Hours
polling_hours.content: New Jersey polling places are open from 6:00 a.m. until 8:00 p.m. on Election Day. A voter who is waiting in line at 8:00 p.m. must be allowed to vote.
polling_hours.source_name: New Jersey Division of Elections — 3 Ways to Vote
polling_hours.internal_note: The Division of Elections directly identifies Election Day voting hours as 6:00 a.m.-8:00 p.m. The 2026 New Jersey Voters' Bill of Rights separately confirms the right of voters already in line at closing time to cast a ballot.

early_voting.label: Early In-Person Voting
early_voting.content: New Jersey provides in-person early voting using voting machines for registered voters before Primary and General Elections. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, early voting runs from Saturday, October 24 through Sunday, November 1. Early-voting locations are open from at least 10:00 a.m. until 8:00 p.m. Monday through Saturday and from at least 10:00 a.m. until 6:00 p.m. on Sundays. No appointment is necessary. A voter may use any designated early-voting location within the voter's county.
early_voting.source_name: New Jersey Division of Elections — In-Person Early Voting
early_voting.internal_note: The Division of Elections directly establishes the October 24-November 1 period, Monday-Saturday 10:00 a.m.-8:00 p.m. hours, Sunday 10:00 a.m.-6:00 p.m. hours, no-appointment rule and countywide use of designated early-voting locations. Counties designate a minimum of three to ten early-voting locations depending on county size.

absentee_mail.label: Vote-by-Mail
absentee_mail.content: Every active registered New Jersey voter is eligible to request a mail-in ballot without providing an excuse. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, counties begin mailing ballots by September 19. A request to receive a mail-in ballot through the mail must be received by the County Clerk by October 27. A voter may apply in person at the County Clerk's office until 3:00 p.m. on November 2. A completed ballot returned through the mail must be postmarked on or before Election Day and received by the County Board of Elections by November 9. A ballot returned to an authorized drop box or delivered in person to the County Board of Elections must arrive by 8:00 p.m. on Election Day. Vote-by-mail ballots cannot be returned at an Election Day polling place or early-voting location.
absentee_mail.glance_value: No excuse; mail request deadline October 27
absentee_mail.source_name: New Jersey Division of Elections — Vote-By-Mail
absentee_mail.internal_note: The current 2026 Vote-By-Mail page directly establishes September 19 as commencement of mailing, October 27 as the mail-application deadline, November 2 at 3:00 p.m. as the in-person application deadline and November 9 as the receipt deadline for timely postmarked ballots. A USPS-delivered ballot without a determinable postmark can still count if received within 48 hours after polls close. Drop-box and hand-delivered ballots must arrive by 8:00 p.m. Election Day.

voter_id.label: Voter ID Requirements
voter_id.content: New Jersey does not generally require an already-registered voter to show identification simply to vote at a polling place. Certain first-time voters must show identification if they registered by mail after January 1, 2003, are voting for the first time in a federal election in that county and did not provide the required identification during registration. Accepted documents for these voters include qualifying photo identification or specified documents showing the voter's name and address. Voters subject to this requirement who cannot provide acceptable identification may use the provisional-ballot procedure provided by state law.
voter_id.glance_value: No general voter ID requirement; limited first-time-voter rule
voter_id.source_name: New Jersey Division of Elections — 2026 Voters' Bill of Rights
voter_id.internal_note: New Jersey should not be described as a universal voter-ID state. The official 2026 Voters' Bill of Rights limits the polling-place ID requirement primarily to certain first-time federal-election voters whose identity was not previously verified. This is the federal HAVA identification procedure. Avoid implying every voter needs a driver's license or photo ID.

accessible_voting.label: Accessible Voting
accessible_voting.content: New Jersey provides accessibility protections for voters with disabilities at polling places and early-voting locations. Election officials are required to address polling-place accessibility, and accommodations are available for voters with disabilities. Voters who encounter an accessibility problem may report it through the Division of Elections' polling-place accessibility process. The state's voting information hotline also provides assistance, and TTY/TDD service is available.
accessible_voting.glance_value: Accessible voting and disability assistance available
accessible_voting.source_name: New Jersey Division of Elections — Voter Rights and Accessibility
accessible_voting.internal_note: The Division of Elections maintains a dedicated accessibility page, complaint form and county accessibility review process. Current 2026 voting guidance expressly states that accommodations will be made for voters with disabilities during both early voting and Election Day voting. State voting assistance is available at 1-877-NJ-VOTER and TTY/TDD 609-292-0034.

military_overseas.label: Military & Overseas Voting
military_overseas.content: New Jersey provides special registration and ballot procedures for eligible military voters, qualifying spouses and dependents, and U.S. citizens living overseas. Covered voters may use the Federal Post Card Application to register and request a ballot. New Jersey permits eligible military and overseas voters to request and receive ballots electronically and to return ballots by electronic transmission under the state's special procedures. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, October 30 is the deadline to apply to receive a mail-in ballot electronically. Military and overseas voters should follow the state's dedicated procedures because registration, transmission and ballot-return requirements differ from ordinary domestic vote-by-mail rules.
military_overseas.glance_value: FPCA and electronic ballot transmission available
military_overseas.source_name: New Jersey Division of Elections — Military and Overseas Voting
military_overseas.internal_note: The Division of Elections directly states that covered military and overseas voters can request and return ballots through electronic transmission by fax or email attachment. The official 2026 voter calendar identifies October 30 as the deadline for an application to receive the General Election ballot electronically. The state's page also provides FPCA and federal voting-assistance resources. Do not apply ordinary domestic vote-by-mail procedures without checking the UOCAVA rules.

student_voting.label: College / Student Voting
student_voting.content: College students may register in New Jersey if they meet the state's voter eligibility and residency requirements. A student who establishes a qualifying New Jersey residence may register using that address. Students who maintain a qualifying voting residence elsewhere may vote according to the rules applicable to that residence. New Jersey provides dedicated student voter registration resources, including online registration and county-specific paper registration forms. A voter should maintain only one voting residence for an election.
student_voting.source_name: New Jersey Division of Elections — Register to Vote
student_voting.internal_note: The Division of Elections registration page directly provides a Student Registration resource and links students to online and county paper registration options. New Jersey's general registration rule requires 30 days of county residence before the election. The reader-facing language avoids implying that attending a New Jersey college automatically establishes New Jersey voting residence.

sample_ballot.label: Official Sample Ballot
sample_ballot.content: New Jersey counties mail sample ballots to eligible voters before the General Election. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, the statewide election timeline lists October 21 as the mailing date for General Election sample ballots. The sample ballot includes voter-specific election information and the voter's Election Day polling location. Because ballot contents depend on the voter's election district, voters should use the sample ballot issued for their address.
sample_ballot.glance_value: General Election sample ballots mailed October 21
sample_ballot.source_name: New Jersey Division of Elections — 2026 General Election Timeline
sample_ballot.internal_note: The official 2026 General Election Timeline establishes October 21 as the mailing date for sample ballots. The polling-location page confirms that a voter's Election Day polling place appears on the sample ballot. The November ballot itself should still be reverified after final candidate and ballot-question certification.

contact.label: Contact the State Election Authority
contact.content: New Jersey Division of Elections. Mailing address: P.O. Box 304, Trenton, NJ 08625-0304. Office address: 225 West State Street, 1st Floor, Trenton, NJ 08608. Phone: 609-292-3760 or 609-789-0124. Voting Information and Assistance: 1-877-NJ-VOTER (1-877-658-6837). TTY/TDD: 609-292-0034. Email: nj.elections@sos.nj.gov. For voter-specific registration, vote-by-mail or polling-place questions, voters may also contact their county election officials.
contact.internal_note: Current Division of Elections pages verify the P.O. Box 304 mailing address, 225 West State Street office address, 609-292-3760 and 609-789-0124 telephone numbers, 609-777-1280 fax, [nj.elections@sos.nj.gov](mailto:nj.elections@sos.nj.gov) email, 1-877-NJ-VOTER assistance line and 609-292-0034 TTY/TDD number. The email address is intentionally plain text with no Markdown or mailto wrapper.

official_resources.label: Official State & Local Resources
official_resources.content: Use the New Jersey Division of Elections Voter Information Portal for official statewide voting information. The portal provides voter registration, registration lookup, polling-place information, early-voting locations, secure ballot drop boxes, vote-by-mail information, ballot tracking, military and overseas voting resources, accessibility information and county election contacts. County election officials administer many voter-specific election functions.
